response.answer: Deep Koopman predictive control effectively mitigates traffic oscillations in mixed traffic by using adaptive data-driven models and real-time control of connected automated vehicles. It enhances traffic flow stability through integration with machine learning techniques. The approach linearizes human-driven vehicle dynamics for better scalability.

The framework features a novel deep Koopman network, AdapKoopnet, which represents complex HDV car-following dynamics as a linear sys-tem in a high-dimensional space by adaptively learning from naturalistic data.

results.title: The impact of selfish driving behavior of autonomous vehicles on mixed traffic flow - ScienceDirect
results.content: # The impact of selfish driving behavior of autonomous vehicles on mixed traffic flow. To investigate the impact of the selfish driving behavior of AVs on the characteristics of mixed traffic flow, this paper proposes a cellular automata model that considers the selfish driving behavior of AVs. First, we analyze the vehicle types‌ in the current mixed traffic flow and develop a universal safety distance model. This model can not only describe the longitudinal car-following and lateral lane-changing behavior of human-driven vehicles and AVs, but also characterize the selfish degree in the driving behavior of AVs. Finally, simulation experiments are designed to analyze the impact of the selfish driving behavior of AVs on the performance indicators of mixed traffic flow. The results show that: (1) The increase in the penetration rate of AVs has a positive effect on the average velocity, traffic stability, and throughput of mixed traffic flow; (2) On the whole, the selfish lane-changing behavior of AVs has a relatively small impact on the average velocity of mixed traffic flow.
